name: Casimir Oyelaran-Devereaux
description: Casimir Oyelaran-Devereaux is the closest thing neural-feed cinema has to a founding legend — a Nigerian-Creole performer from Chicago's Tier 3 mid-stack who appeared in over sixty neural productions between 2183 and 2218, working for every major studio and several independent ones before Vantablack consolidated enough of the industry to make that impossible. His neural signature is described by feed architects as 'architecturally generous' — audiences inhabiting his performances report a quality of expanded spatial awareness combined with deep ethical gravity that no other performer has replicated. Now in his late sixties, he is partially retired but remains a Vantablack contract consultant.
cultural_impact: Oyelaran-Devereaux's career spans the entire history of neural-feed as a mature art form, and his performances are used as benchmark reference material in every serious neural-feed production school in Meridian 88.
story_hooks: Oyelaran-Devereaux reaches out to someone outside Vantablack with a request: he wants his full unedited neural archive copied before his contract's termination clause allows Vantablack to control it posthumously.
A young actor whose neural signature bears an uncanny resemblance to Oyelaran-Devereaux's is being fast-tracked by Vantablack — and Oyelaran-Devereaux believes the resemblance is not coincidental.
The original unedited version of his 2216 interview contains more than a critical comment — it contains specific allegations he chose to cut himself, and someone wants to know what he didn't say.
